engagement_background.objective: Create measurable procurement cost savings by leveraging APDerm’s enterprise-wide purchasing power across indirect spend categories, supporting Waud Capital’s value-creation plan while ensuring business needs and service levels were maintained.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Two-phase strategic sourcing engagement addressing roughly $6.3 million in annual, addressable spend across 10+ indirect categories (e.g., Billing Services, Janitorial Services, IT Managed Services, Laundry/Linen, Non-IT Temp Labor, Copier/Print, Uniforms, Medical & Office Supplies). Waste Management was later removed from scope due to limited savings viability; direct clinical revenue-generating costs were not included.
constraints_challenges: Decentralized, multi-site purchasing after years of acquisitive growth created a fragmented supplier base with limited leverage.
Poor spend visibility and data quality—vendor names required extensive deduplication and GL mapping; some supplier usage data was incomplete or unresponsive.
Inflationary environment and pandemic-related supply-chain disruptions drove upward price pressure during the project.
Long-standing incumbent relationships made stakeholders sensitive to supplier changes and reduced switching credibility.
Private-equity timeline pressured rapid sourcing cycles and quick savings realization.

procurement_environment.data_availability: Accounts-payable invoice extracts and GL data were available for a 12-month period; no centralized contract repository; supplier usage data had to be requested individually.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Inconsistent vendor naming, many unmapped categories, and gaps in historical usage data necessitated extensive cleansing, deduplication, and benchmarking before baseline creation.
